S16.01.note: Expected asks for a visible avatar or name; the code shows the author only by bubble alignment and style, with the name visually hidden.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel in the VS Code sidebar.
Type "Hello" in the message box and press Enter.
Look at your message: it is a bubble on the right, with a dashed border while it is sending.
Compare with Expected: the author is shown by alignment and bubble style, but no visible name or avatar appears; the name is only announced to screen readers.
S16.01.where: Chat panel > send any message > look at the right-aligned bubble. There is no visible name or avatar; the author label "You said:" is screen-reader text only (webviewContent.ts 5771).

steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Type "Hello, list the files here" in the message box.
Press Enter.
Look at the right-aligned bubble: the same text should appear exactly as typed.
S16.02.where: Chat panel > type a message and press Enter > the bubble shows your text.

S16.03.note: The exact menu item for picking a file was not confirmed from the + menu; the code has "Attach workspace files" and "Attach file…" text in different places.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Click the + button ("Attach or use tools") above the message box and attach a file or image.
Check that the file chip shows in the strip above the message box.
Type a message and press Enter.
Look under your bubble: the file is listed as a chip named after the file (with an icon). Compare with Expected.
S16.03.where: Chat panel > + (Attach or use tools) > attach a file, then send > chips appear under your bubble.

S16.04.note: Quoted text, page and @mention chips were not traced to a control in this pass; only the Browse the web chip and editor context strip were confirmed.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Click the + button ("Attach or use tools") and turn on "Browse the web".
Type a message and press Enter.
Look under your bubble: a "Browse the web" chip appears, and a Context (count) toggle lists the non-file context when it was sent.
S16.04.where: Chat panel > + (Attach or use tools) > turn on Browse the web > send > the sent message shows a Context chip list.

S16.09.note: The button is icon-only; its word "Resend" is the tooltip and accessible name.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel and send a message, then wait for the reply.
Move the pointer over your message bubble so the action icons appear under it.
Hover the redo-arrow icon to see the tooltip "Resend", then click it.
Look at the transcript: a new reply comes back for the same unchanged text, with a new message entry.
S16.09.where: Chat panel > hover over your sent message > click the Resend icon (redo arrow) on the message.

S16.10.needs: a conversation with at least two turns
S16.10.note: Code shows a new session with the message placed in the composer for editing, not a sent copy of the thread; the exact thread contents were not confirmed.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel and send two or more messages with replies.
Move the pointer over an earlier message bubble and hover the fork icon to see the tooltip "Branch".
Click it.
Look at the result: a new session opens with the message ready to edit in the message box; the first message starts a fresh conversation.
S16.10.where: Chat panel > hover over your sent message > click the Branch icon (fork icon) on the message.

S16.14.note: The state may last under a second on a fast connection, so the tester may need a slow network or a long wait to see it.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Type a message and press Enter.
Look immediately under your bubble for the caption "Sending".
Compare with Expected: the caption should change once the service accepts the message.
S16.14.where: Chat panel > send a message > look under your bubble for "Sending" until the service accepts it.

S16.15.needs: a way to make a send fail
S16.15.note: The code does not say which action causes the failure; the tester needs a method for it.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel.
Cause a failed send, such as losing the network or signing out, then type a message and press Enter.
Look under the bubble for "Not sent" in the error colour.
Look below the transcript for the error block with a "Retry" button.
S16.15.where: Chat panel > send a message that fails > look under your bubble for "Not sent" and the red error block.

S16.16.needs: a way to make a send fail, and an attachment for the attachment check
S16.16.note: The Retry button appears only when the error is marked retryable; attachment re-sending was not confirmed from the code.
steps: Make a send fail as in S16.15.
Click the "Retry" button in the error block under the transcript.
Look: the error block disappears and the same text is sent again with a new reply.
Compare with Expected: the failure should be replaced by the new outcome; check the attachments are still listed on the message.
S16.16.where: Chat panel > after a failed send, click "Retry" in the error block.

S16.17.note: The follow-up behaviour (Queue or Steer) is a setting; the Steer path shows "Steered" instead of waiting.
steps: Open the AGI chat panel and send a long request so a reply starts streaming.
While the reply is still running, type a second message and press Enter (the button beside Stop reads "Queue" or "Steer").
Look under the new bubble for "Queued" with Edit and Cancel icons.
Wait for the first reply to finish: the "Queued" caption should clear and the message should go out.
S16.17.where: Chat panel > send a message while a reply is still running > look under the new bubble for "Queued".
